title: Unhandled exceptions in token loading and Bot construction bypass the friendly error path
reasoning: open()/read() on .env and config.json (lines 16-25) can raise PermissionError/OSError if the files exist but are unreadable, and Bot(token=...) at line 38 raises ValueError/TypeError for a malformed, empty-after-strip, or stale token. All of these run outside the try/except at lines 39-50, so the script aborts with a raw traceback instead of the intended user-facing message, and a constructor failure skips the session-cleanup path entirely. These failure modes are realistic because tokens are read from mutable local files and can be edited or stale.
reproduction: Set TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN to a malformed value such as `not-a-token` and run the script: Bot() raises outside the try block and the process exits with a traceback.
recommendation: Wrap token loading and `bot = Bot(token=token)` inside the existing try/except (or validate the token format before construction) and print the friendly error message on failure; keep session close in a finally that only references bot when construction succeeded.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests exist for the script, so the malformed-token and unreadable-file paths are never exercised.
suggestedRegressionTest: A pytest test that monkeypatches Bot to raise ValueError on construction and asserts main() prints the friendly error instead of propagating a traceback.
